matchups.recap: Rob got absolutely skull-fucked by 19.4 points this week, and honestly, that's what happens when you field a roster that couldn't score in a brothel with a fistful of cash. You limped across the finish line at 96.5 like a guy who just discovered his entire bench was on bye week, while Ben flexed 115.9 and left you wondering where the hell your "studs" went. Better luck next week, you absolute donkey.

Nori showed up to this matchup like he showed up to the draft—completely fucking unprepared and wondering why everything fell apart by halftime. Down 23.7 points, Nori's roster looked like a clearance bin at a thrift store, with every player underperforming like they had money on the other team. Veton didn't even need to break a sweat; he just sat back and watched Nori's season implode in real time like a highlight reel of pure fantasy incompetence. Better luck next year, chief—or actually, keep doing exactly what you're doing so we can all keep laughing.

Faton got absolutely cock-teased this week, limping across the finish line 4.6 points short like a guy who thought he had it in the bag and then remembered he left his wallet at home. 109 points should be enough to win most weeks, but apparently not when you're facing Arben, who managed to scrape together 113.6 points of pure, unapologetic fantasy football competence. Faton's roster had all the makings of a championship run until it didn't—kind of like watching a Ferrari with no gas tank. Better luck next week, chief, because this loss is gonna sting like whiskey on a paper cut.

Ilir got absolutely obliterated this week, losing by 27.7 points like he was trying to tank for draft picks. His roster put up 77.9 points of pure dogshit, which is what happens when your "strategy" is apparently to autodraft players who've been injured since 2019. Flamur waltzed into the endzone with 104.6 while Ilir's team choked harder than a rookie QB in the playoffs, and now he's got nothing but excuses and a bye week to contemplate his garbage life choices.

Jetmir and Peter got so close to stealing this one they could taste it—too bad they choked it down like a two-minute drill led by a rookie. Losing by 2.8 points is the fantasy football equivalent of showing up to a gunfight with a butter knife: technically you tried, but everyone watching just felt bad. Rinor walked out with the W while you two were left arguing about whose draft pick was worse, and spoiler alert—it doesn't matter because you both shit the bed this week.

Rilind got absolutely skull-fucked by 23.6 points this week, limping across the finish line like a three-legged dog with a score that wouldn't embarrass a bye week. Adam went full on weekend warrior and left you in the dust while your roster looked like you drafted it at a fucking bus stop. Better luck next week, chief—though honestly, I wouldn't count on it.

matchups.preview: Rob's clinging to a .286 winning percentage like it's a participation trophy, but Veton's here to remind him that 1-6 is somehow even more pathetic—this is a race to the bottom between two teams that make you wonder if they even set their lineups. One of these dumpster fires is going down 0-7, and honestly, does it even matter which one at this point?

Faton's sitting pretty at 4-3 thinking he's got this locked down, but we all remember how last year ended—choking harder than a rookie in the playoffs. Ben's desperate at 3-4 and has nothing to lose, which means he's either going to pull off the upset or continue his season-long tradition of starting the wrong guys. Either way, one of these clowns is about to get exposed this week.

Two mediocre bastards limping along at .500 are about to find out which one is actually worse—and spoiler alert, Ilir, your "balanced approach" is just code for "I panic-started three guys who combined for 8 points last week." Nori's at least been consistently mid all season, but you? You've got all the talent in the world and somehow still managed to lose to half this league. One of you is about to remember what it feels like to actually lose momentum, and my money's on the guy who thought his draft capital could carry him through November.

Jetmir and Peter are about to find out why 4-3 feels a lot worse than it actually is when they run into a 6-1 buzzsaw that knows how to close out games. Arben's been running circles around this league while you two have been trading punches with the middle pack—this week you're just getting knocked the fuck out.

Rilind's bringing a dumpster fire to face the league's hottest team—and honestly, that might be the most entertaining thing his roster's done all season. Flamur's rolling with the kind of momentum that makes 1-6 records look even more pathetic, so expect Rilind to find new and creative ways to lose while watching his studs underperform on the bench. This isn't a matchup; it's a mercy killing.

Adam's sitting at 3-4 with a roster that screams "I panic-drafted and never looked back," while Rinor limps in at 4-3 probably wondering how the fuck he's still this close to .500 with the mid-tier garbage he's been fielding. This is the matchup of two dudes desperately trying not to fall out of contention, which means one of you is about to absolutely implode and waste your Sunday afternoon watching your team score 60 points.
